intended_object: The identity morphism of an object (X_i)_{i∈ι} in the matrix category Mat_(C) (the additive envelope of a preadditive category C). It is the matrix with 𝟙_{X_i} on the diagonal and 0 off the diagonal, as the docstring says and as the `Category (Mat_ C)` instance uses it.
explanation: A morphism M ⟶ N in Mat_ C is a dependent matrix of morphisms M.X i ⟶ N.X j. The definition sets entry (i, j) to `eqToHom` when i = j and to 0 otherwise. When i = j, `eqToHom` of `M.X i = M.X i` is definitionally the identity; this is the standard dependent-type way to state "identity on the diagonal". So the definition is exactly the identity matrix. Classical decidable equality on the index type is harmless here. The library's `id_def` lemma and the `id_comp`/`comp_id` proofs in the category instance confirm it acts as the identity for matrix composition. The definition is at its natural generality: it needs only zero morphisms, which a preadditive category has, and a finite index type, which is how Mat_ is defined. Mathlib has no separate general version of this construction, so there is no counterpart.
